title: Rabbi Zeira bar Chanina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Niddah 3b, resolving the Gemara’s difficulty. Hyman suggests that he is called Ze’or or Ze’ir bar Chinena in the Jerusalem Talmud. In Berakhot 5:1: “Ze’or bar Chinena said: one who lets blood from consecrated [animals] commits misappropriation”; also Shabbat 7:2, 30a, and there, end of halakhah 4. In Sanhedrin, beginning of chapter 4, he reported in Rabbi Chanina’s name; in Avodah Zarah 4:5, in Rabbi Chananiah’s name (Rabbi Chanina, the Rabbis’ colleague).

And in Terumot, end of ch. 8, it is related that once he was captured by bandits, and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Shemuel went to Zenobia the queen to intercede on his behalf, and through a miracle he was saved.

notes.text: Hyman tentatively identifies the Bavli and Jerusalem Talmud name forms. חברון דרבנן means the Rabbis’ colleague, not a further personal name.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:54 and Sanhedrin 4:1:2 directly name Ze’ir bar Chinena transmitting in Rabbi Chanina’s name. They do not establish his identity with the supplied Bavli Zeira bar Chanina. The supplied Niddah 3b and Berakhot 5:1 loci were not independently matched in the bounded passages consulted; no absence is inferred. The identification and miracle narrative remain Hyman’s report.
